Sunaina's mother had set it up through a family friend, so Sunaina went to the café in Koregaon Park expecting to be polite for an hour and leave.
Vikas turned out to be funny. He did a wicked impression of his manager and admitted he'd spent the whole morning choosing a shirt. She laughed more than she'd planned.
But under the laughter, a list kept running. He'd mentioned a possible transfer to Singapore next year. She had just been made team lead in Pune and loved it. He talked about "settling down soon"; she wanted two more years before thinking about marriage at all.
When the bill came, he asked, "Can I see you again?" She felt a real flutter, and at the same moment a small, practical voice asking, And then what?
"Yes," she said. "But I have questions. Real ones."
"Good," Vikas said. "So do I."

qa.q: Where might Vikas be transferred next year?
qa.a: Vikas mentioned a possible transfer to Singapore next year.

qa.q: What two feelings did Sunaina have when Vikas asked to meet again?
qa.a: Sunaina felt a real flutter of excitement and, at the same moment, a cautious, practical voice asking, "And then what?"

qa.q: What is wise about Sunaina's answer 'Yes, but I have questions'?
qa.a: It lets her follow the attraction while being honest that career, city and timing matter, so both can talk openly from the start.

qa.q: How might Vikas feel about Sunaina having real questions?
qa.a: Vikas seems relieved, since he says he has questions too; he also seems to want honesty rather than just a pleasant evening.

grounding: Shows a young professional meeting someone through family, with attraction and practical questions about career, city and timing in the same evening.

"So? How was she?" Suraj didn't even let Naveen get through the door.
"Keerthi? Nice. Really nice, actually."
"Nice-nice, or Amma's-friend's-daughter nice?"
"Nice-nice. She laughed at my bad joke about the traffic. And she's reading the same book I am."
"So it's fixed! I'll tell Amma."
"Don't you dare. She's doing her PhD in Bengaluru for three more years. My job is here in Chennai. And she said, straight out, that she won't move for someone she's known for a month."
"Fair."
"Very fair. That's what I liked. She asked what I want in five years. Nobody's asked me that."
"And what do you want?"
Naveen dropped onto the sofa. "I think... I want to see her again. And I also want to not get ahead of myself."
"Both?"
"Both."

qa.q: How long will Keerthi be doing her PhD in Bengaluru?
qa.a: Keerthi is doing her PhD in Bengaluru for three more years.

qa.q: What mixed feelings does Naveen have after meeting Keerthi?
qa.a: Naveen is excited and wants to see Keerthi again, but is also cautious about the distance and about getting ahead of things.

qa.q: Why was Keerthi's question about five years a good sign?
qa.a: It showed Keerthi was thinking about fit, not just the evening, which gives Naveen a chance to talk honestly about goals early on.

qa.q: How does Suraj see the evening?
qa.a: Suraj is eager to call it fixed and tell Amma, seeing the romance before the practical questions Naveen is weighing.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional after a family-arranged meeting, feeling real attraction alongside caution about city, career and readiness.

passage:
You're nervous about meeting that boy your mother found, beta? Let me, your Noor khala, tell you about the evening I met Harish.

Friends set it up. A dinner at their flat in Delhi, very casual, they said. I was twenty-five, working at the bank, and I had decided I was not moving cities for any man.

He was charming. He made me laugh twice before the soup. I liked his hands, and how he listened. My heart was doing silly things.

But I also asked him, straight out, where he saw himself in five years. Bombay, he said, for his work. My stomach sank a little. I asked if he wanted his wife to work. He said, "That's her choice." That helped.

I went home both excited and wary. That's what I want you to know: feeling both is not a bad sign. It means your heart and your head are both at the table.

qa.q: Where did Noor khala meet Harish?
qa.a: At a dinner at their friends' flat in Delhi.

qa.q: How did Noor feel when Harish said he saw himself in Bombay?
qa.a: Her stomach sank a little; she felt worried, since she had decided not to move cities, even while she was attracted to him.

qa.q: What choice inside the story helped Noor judge the match wisely?
qa.a: Asking Harish directly about the future and about work, so her excitement was balanced by practical answers.

qa.q: How might Harish have felt when Noor asked such direct questions?
qa.a: He may have been surprised, but perhaps impressed and relieved to talk honestly so early.

grounding: Noor khala recalls meeting Harish through friends, feeling attraction and practical caution about career and city on the same evening.

The meeting was supposed to be at a café in Porto, but the storm knocked out the power, so Anand and Maria ended up drinking coffee by candlelight in the café's back room, arranged by his aunt's friend, who was Maria's neighbour.

He'd been nervous all day. She was lovely: sharp, funny, with paint on her sleeve from her studio. By the second coffee he was hoping the storm would last.

But he also had questions. He worked in Mumbai and was only in Portugal for six months. She had just opened her studio here.

"So," she said, reading his face, "you're wondering which city."

"I am," he admitted. "And whether you'd ever want to move."

"I don't know yet. Would you?"

He didn't know either.

When the lights came back, he felt both excited and cautious, like someone standing at the edge of the sea.

qa.q: Why did Anand and Maria end up drinking coffee by candlelight?
qa.a: The storm knocked out the power.

qa.q: How did Anand feel by the end of the evening?
qa.a: He felt excited and attracted to Maria, but also cautious about their different cities and futures.

qa.q: What small step might help them at this stage?
qa.a: Keep meeting while being honest about the city question, so they learn whether it can work without rushing.

qa.q: What might Maria be thinking when she reads his face?
qa.a: She is likely curious and a little wary herself, weighing her new studio against the chance of something with him.

grounding: Anand and Maria's storm-lit meeting shows attraction tempered by practical questions of city and career, with excitement and caution in the same evening.

passage:
The two families had arranged it at Bidisha's aunt's flat in Salt Lake, Kolkata: tea, sandesh, and the usual careful small talk. Then the parents found reasons to leave Bidisha and Anirban alone on the balcony.

She'd expected to be bored. Instead Anirban made her laugh about his mother's fifty text messages that morning. He had nice eyes and a way of pausing before he answered, as if the question mattered.

She liked him. That surprised her.

But she had questions too. She was up for a promotion in Pune. He worked in Kolkata and his parents expected him to stay.

"Would you ever move?" she asked.

"For the right reason, maybe. Would you ever move back?"

"I'm not sure."

When the families returned, Bidisha felt a flutter she hadn't expected and a small knot of worry sitting right beside it.

qa.q: Where was the meeting arranged?
qa.a: At Bidisha's aunt's flat in Salt Lake, Kolkata.

qa.q: What does Bidisha feel at the end of the meeting?
qa.a: She feels an unexpected flutter of excitement and a knot of worry about the career and city question.

qa.q: Which choice helped Bidisha, and why?
qa.a: Asking Anirban directly about moving helped, because it brought the practical question into the open early.

qa.q: How might Anirban feel about Bidisha's promotion in Pune?
qa.a: He may feel interested but uneasy, since his parents expect him to stay in Kolkata.

grounding: At a family-arranged meeting, Bidisha is attracted to Anirban but cautious about career and city, so excitement and worry share the evening.

passage:
"So Nirmala Aunty told you I'm a data analyst who reads too much?" Alka asked.
"She said you'd grill me," Sameer grinned. "Go on."
"Fine. You're in Bengaluru. My job is in Pune and I just got promoted. Would you move, or would I be expected to?"
"Honestly? I don't know yet. I like my team. But I wouldn't expect you to move just because you're the woman."
Alka laughed, then caught herself enjoying it a little too much. "And children? My mother already has names picked."
"Mine too," he said. "Not before thirty, for me. Is that a problem?"
"No. It's actually a relief." She stirred her coffee. "I'm having fun. That's what worries me."
"Why?"
"Because fun is easy. City, career, being ready, those are the hard parts."
"Then let's meet again," Sameer said, "and talk about the hard parts properly."

qa.q: Where is Alka's job?
qa.a: Alka's job is in Pune, where she just got promoted.

qa.q: Why does Alka say that having fun is what worries her?
qa.a: She is excited by Sameer's company but cautious, afraid that the easy fun might hide the hard questions about city, career and being ready.

qa.q: What is a wise next step for Alka at this early stage?
qa.a: Meeting again, as Sameer suggests, while keeping the practical questions on the table, lets her test the spark against real plans instead of one pleasant evening.

qa.q: How might Sameer be feeling when Alka asks whether he would move?
qa.a: He may feel put on the spot but also respected, since he answers honestly that he does not know yet and seems to enjoy her directness.

grounding: Shows a young professional introduced through family feeling real attraction alongside careful questions about career, city and readiness.
